r00101-00104 p003   T hath been the wiſdom of the Church of England, ever ſince the firſt compiling of her Publick Liturgy, to keep
r00105-00107 p003   the mean between the two extremes, of too much ſtiffneſs
r00108-00120 p003   in refuſing, and of too much eaſineſs in admitting any variation from it. For, as on the one ſide common experience ſheweth, that where a change hath been made of things adviſedly eſtabliſhed (no evident neceſſity ſo requiring) ſundry inconveniences have thereupon enſued; and thoſe
r00121-00124 p003   many times more and greater than the evils, that were intended to be remedied by ſuch change: So on the other ſide, the particular Forms of Divine Worſhip, and the Rites
r00125-00126 p003   and Ceremonies appointed to be uſed therein, being things
r00127-00129 p003   in their own nature indifferent, and alterable, and ſo acknowledged; it is but reaſonable, that upon weighty and
r00130-00135 p003   important conſiderations, according to the various exigency of times and occaſions, ſuch Changes and Alterations ſhould be made therein, as to thoſe that are in place of
r00136-00138 p003   Authority ſhould from time to time ſeem either neceſſary or
r00139-00141 p003   expedient. Accordingly we find, that in the Reigns of ſeveral Princes of bleſſed memory ſince the Reformation, the
r00142-00148 p003   Church, upon juſt and weighty conſiderations her thereunto moving, hath yielded to make ſuch Alterations in ſome particulars, as in their reſponſive times were thought
r00149-00150 p003   convenient: Yet ſo, as that the main Body and Eſſentials of
r00151-00152 p003   it (as well in the chiefeſt Materials, as in the frame and
r00153-00155 p003   order thereof) have ſtill continued the ſame unto this day,
r00156-00159 p003   and do yet ſtand firm and unſhaken, notwithſtanding all
r00160-00161 p003   the vain attempts and impetuous aſſaults made againſt it,
r00162-00163 p003   by ſuch men as are given to change, and have always
r00164-00165 p003   diſcovered a greater regard to their own private fancies and
r00166-00167 p003   intereſts, than to that duty they owe to the publick.
r00168-00171 p003    By what undue means, and for what miſchievous purpoſes the uſe of the Liturgy (though enjoined by the Laws
r00172-00172 p003 D I
r00174-00174 p004   The P R E F A C E.
r00175-00176 p004   of the Land, and thoſe Laws never yet repealed) came,
r00177-00179 p004   during the late unhappy confuſions, to be diſcontinued, is
r00180-00184 p004   too well known to the world, and we are not willing here to remember. But when, upon His Majeſty’s happy Reſtoration, it ſeemed probable, that, amongſt other things, the
r00185-00189 p004   uſe of the Liturgy alſo would return of courſe (the ſame
r00190-00192 p004   having never been legally aboliſhed) unleſs ſome timely
r00193-00195 p004   means were uſed to prevent it; thoſe men who under the
r00196-00204 p004   late uſurped powers had made it a great part of their buſineſs to render the people diſaffected thereunto, ſaw themſelves in point of reputation and intereſt concerned (unleſs
r00205-00206 p004   they would freely acknowledge themſelves to have erred,
r00207-00208 p004   which ſuch men are very hardly brought to do) with their
r00209-00211 p004   utmoſt endeavours to hinder the reſtitution thereof. In
r00212-00214 p004   order whereunto divers Pamphlets were publiſhed againſt
r00215-00216 p004   the Book of Common Prayer, the old Objections mustered
r00217-00218 p004   up, with the addition of ſome new ones, more than
r00219-00220 p004   formerly had been made, to make the number ſwell. In
r00221-00223 p004   fine, great importunities were uſed to His Sacred Majeſty,
r00224-00227 p004   that the ſaid Book might be reviſed, and ſuch Alterations
r00228-00229 p004   therein, and Additions thereunto made, as ſhould be
r00230-00247 p004   thought requiſite for the eaſe of tender Conſciences: whereunto His Majeſty, out of his pious inclination to give ſatiſfaction (ſo far as could be reaſonably expected) to all his ſubjects of what perſuaſion ſoever, did graciouſly condeſcend.
r00248-00249 p004    In which Review we have endeavoured to obſerve the
r00250-00251 p004   like moderation, as we find to have been uſed in the like
r00252-00257 p004   caſe in former times. And therefore of the ſundry Alterations propoſed unto us, we have rejected all ſuch as were
r00258-00266 p004   either of dangerous conſequence (as ſecretly ſtriking at ſome eſtabliſhed doctrine, or laudable practice of the
r00267-00267 p004   Church of England, or indeed of the whole Catholick
r00268-00271 p004   Church of Chriſt) or elſe of no conſequence at all, but
r00272-00274 p004   utterly frivolous and vain. But ſuch alterations as were tendered to us, (by what perſons, under what pretences, or to
r00275-00278 p004   what purpoſe ſoever tendered) as ſeemed to us in any
r00279-00280 p004   degree requiſite or expedient, we have willingly, and of our
r00281-00282 p004   own accord aſſented unto: Not enforced ſo to do by any
r00283-00284 p004   The P R E F A C E. ſtrength of Argument, convincing us of the neceſſity of
r00285-00287 p004   making the ſaid Alterations: For we are fully perſuaded in
r00288-00289 p004   our judgements (and we here profeſs it to the world) that
r00290-00293 p004   the Book, as it ſtood before eſtabliſhed by Law, doth not
r00294-00295 p004   contain in it any thing contrary to the Word of God, or to ſound Doctrine, or which a godly man may not with a good
r00296-00299 p004   Conſcience uſe and ſubmit unto, or which is not fairly
r00300-00306 p004   defenſible againſt any that ſhall oppoſe the ſame; if it ſhall
r00307-00311 p004   be allowed ſuch juſt and favourable conſtruction as in
r00312-00314 p004   common equity ought to be allowed to all human Writings, eſpecially ſuch as are ſet forth by Authority, and even to
r00315-00318 p004   the very beſt Tranſlations of the holy Scripture itſelf.
r00319-00320 p004    Our general aim therefore in this undertaking was, not to gratify this or that party in any their unreaſonable
r00321-00323 p004   demands; but to do that, which to our beſt underſtandings
r00324-00326 p004   we conceived might moſt tend to the preſervation of Peace
r00327-00328 p004   and Unity in the Church; the procuring of Reverence, and exciting of Piety and Devotion in the publick Worſhip of
r00329-00333 p004   God; and the cutting off occaſion from them that ſeek occaſion of cavil or quarrel againſt the Liturgy of the Church.
r00334-00335 p004   And as to the ſeveral variations from the former Book,
r00336-00342 p004   whether by Alteration, Addition, or otherwiſe, it ſhall ſuffice to give this general account. That moſt of the Alterations were made, either firſt, for the better direction of
r00343-00344 p004   them that are to officiate in any part of Divine Service; which is chiefly done in the Calendars and Rubricks: Or ſecondly, for the more proper expreſſing of ſome words or
r00345-00356 p004   phraſes of ancient uſage in terms more ſuitable to the language of the preſent times, and the clearer explanation of ſome other words and phraſes, that were either of doubtful ſignification, or otherwiſe liable to miſconſtruction: Or
r00357-00359 p004   thirdly, for a more perfect rendering of ſuch portions of
r00360-00361 p004   holy Scripture, as are inſerted into the Liturgy; which, in
r00362-00366 p004   the Epiſtles and Goſpels eſpecially, and in ſundry other
r00367-00368 p004   places, are now ordered to be read according to the laſt
r00369-00371 p004   Tranſlation: and that it was thought convenient, that ſome
r00372-00377 p004   Prayers and Thankſgivings, fitted to ſpecial occaſions, ſhould be added in their due places; particularly for thoſe
r00379-00379 p005 H Concerning the Service of the C H U R C H .
r00380-00382 p005   at Sea, together with an Office for the Baptiſm of ſuch as
r00383-00384 p005   are of Riper Years: which, although not ſo neceſſary when
r00385-00388 p005   the former Book was compiled, yet by the growth of Anabaptiſm, through the licentiouſneſs of the late times
r00389-00390 p005   crept in amongſt us, is now become neceſſary, and may be
r00391-00395 p005   always uſeful for the baptizing of Natives in our Plantations, and others converted to the Faith. If any man, who ſhall deſire a more particular account of the ſeveral
r00396-00397 p005   Alterations in any part of the Liturgy, ſhall take the pains
r00398-00399 p005   to compare the preſent Book with the former; we doubt not
r00400-00402 p005   but the reaſon of the change may eaſily appear.
r00403-00404 p005    And having thus endeavoured to diſcharge our duties in
r00405-00406 p005   this weighty Affair, as in the ſight of God, and to approve
r00407-00410 p005   our ſincerity therein (ſo far as lay in us) to the conſciences
r00411-00412 p005   of all men; although we know it impoſſible (in ſuch variety
r00413-00415 p005   of apprehenſions, humours and intereſts, as are in the
r00416-00419 p005   world) to pleaſe all; nor can expect that men of factious,
r00420-00426 p005   peeviſh, and perverſe ſpirits ſhould be ſatiſfied with any
r00427-00428 p005   thing that can be done in this kind by any other than themſelves: Yet we have good hope, that what is here preſented,
r00429-00430 p005   and hath been by the Convocations of both Provinces with great diligence examined and approved, will be alſo well
r00431-00432 p005   accepted and approved by all ſober, peaceable, and truly
r00433-00434 p005   conſcientious Sons of the Church of England.
r00435-00435 p005   ¶ Concerning the Service of the C H U R C H .
r00436-00437 p005   H E R E was never any thing by the wit of man ſo well
r00438-00443 p005   deviſed, or ſo ſure eſtabliſhed, which in contin-uance
r00444-00445 p005   of time hath not been corrupted: As, among other things, it may plainly appear by the Common Prayers in the Church, commonly called Divine Service. The firſt original and
r00446-00447 p005   ground whereof if a man would ſearch out by the ancient
r00448-00450 p005   Fathers, he ſhall find, that the ſame was not ordained but
r00451-00454 p005   of a good purpoſe, and for a great advancement of godlineſs. For they ſo ordered the matter, that all the whole
r00455-00457 p005   Bible (or the greateſt part thereof) ſhould be read over
r00458-00458 p005 D T
r00459-00459 p005 H Concerning the Service of the C H U R C H .
r00460-00464 p005   every year; intending thereby, that the Clergy, and eſpecially ſuch as were Miniſters in the congregation, ſhould
r00465-00466 p005   (by often reading, and meditation in God’s word) be ſtirred
r00467-00469 p005   up to godlineſs themſelves and be more able to exhort others
r00470-00473 p005   by wholeſome Doctrine, and to confute them that were adverſaries to the Truth; and further, that the people (by
r00474-00475 p005   daily hearing of holy Scripture read in the Church) might continually profit more and more in the knowledge of God, and be the more inflamed with the love of his true Religion.  But theſe many years paſſed, this godly and decent order
r00476-00477 p005   of the ancient Fathers hath been ſo altered, broken, and
r00478-00479 p005   neglected, by planting in uncertain Stories, and Legends,
r00480-00482 p005   with multitude of Reſponds, Verſes, vain Repetitions,
r00483-00485 p005   Commemorations, and Synodals; that commonly when any Book of the Bible was begun, after three of four Chapters were read out, all the reſt were unread. And in this ſort the
r00486-00486 p005   Book of
r00487-00487 p005   Iſaiah was begun in Advent, and the Book of Geneſis
r00488-00488 p005   in Septuageſima; but they were only begun, and never read
r00489-00490 p005   through: After like ſort were other Books of holy Scripture
r00491-00494 p005   uſed. And moreover, whereas St. Paul would have ſuch language ſpoken to the people in the Church, as they might
r00495-00499 p005   underſtand, and have profit by hearing the ſame; the ſervice in this Church of England theſe many years hath
r00500-00501 p005   been read in Latin to the people, which they underſtand
r00502-00503 p005   not; ſo that they have heard with their ears only, and their
r00504-00505 p005   heart, ſpirit and mind, have not been edified thereby. And
r00506-00507 p005   furthermore, notwithſtanding that the ancient Fathers have
r00508-00508 p005   divided the
r00509-00510 p005   Pſalms into ſeven portions, whereof every one
r00511-00512 p005   was called a Nocturn: Now of late time a few of them have
r00513-00515 p005   been daily ſaid, and the reſt utterly omitted. Moreover, the
r00516-00517 p005   number and hardneſs of the Rules called the Pie, and the
r00518-00519 p005   manifold changings of the Service, was the cauſe, that to
r00520-00521 p005   turn the Book only was ſo hard and intricate a matter, that
r00522-00525 p005   many times there was more buſineſs to find out what ſhould be read, than to read it when it was found out.
r00526-00529 p005    Theſe inconveniences therefore conſidered, here is ſet
r00530-00533 p005   forth ſuch an Order, whereby the ſame ſhall be redreſſed.
r00534-00535 p005   And for a readineſs in this matter, here is drawn out a Ca-
r00537-00537 p006 H Concerning the Service of the C H U R C H .
r00538-00542 p006   lendar for that purpoſe, which is plain and eaſy to be underſtood; wherein (ſo much as may be) the reading of holy
r00543-00546 p006   Scripture is ſo ſet forth, that all things ſhall be done in
r00547-00550 p006   order, without breaking one piece from another. For this cauſe be cut off Anthems, Reſponds, Invitatories, and ſuch
r00551-00552 p006   like things as did break the continual courſe of the reading
r00553-00554 p006   of the Scripture.  Yet, becauſe there is no remedy, but that of neceſſity
r00555-00559 p006   there muſt be ſome Rules; therefore certain Rules are here ſet forth; which, as they are few in number, ſo they are
r00560-00562 p006   plain and eaſy to be underſtood. So that here you have an
r00563-00564 p006   Order for Prayer, and for the reading of the holy Scripture, much agreeable to the mind and purpoſe of the old Fathers, and a great deal more profitable and commodious,
r00565-00566 p006   than that which of late was uſed. It is more profitable,
r00567-00569 p006   many things, whereof ſome are untrue, becauſe here are left
r00570-00574 p006   out ſome uncertain, ſome vain and ſuperſtitious; and nothing is ordained to be read, but the very pure Word of
r00575-00577 p006   God, the holy Scriptures, or that which is agreeable to the ſame; and that in ſuch a Language and Order as is moſt
r00578-00580 p006   eaſy and plain for the underſtanding both of the Readers
r00581-00585 p006   and Hearers. It is alſo more commodious, both for the ſhortneſs thereof, and for the plainneſs of the order, and
r00586-00587 p006   for that the rules be few and eaſy.
r00588-00589 p006    And whereas heretofore there hath been great diverſity
r00590-00593 p006   in ſaying and ſinging in Churches within this Realm; ſome
r00594-00599 p006   following Saliſbury Uſe, ſome Hereford Uſe, and ſome the Uſe
r00600-00602 p006   of Bangor, ſome of York, ſome of Lincoln; now from henceforth all the whole Realm ſhall have but one Uſe.
r00603-00606 p006    And foraſmuch as nothing can be ſo plainly ſet forth,
r00607-00611 p006   but doubts may ariſe in the uſe and practice of the ſame; to
r00612-00617 p006   appeaſe all ſuch diverſity (if any ariſe) and for the reſolution of all doubts, concerning the manner how to underſtand, do, and execute, the things contained in this Book;
r00618-00621 p006   the parties that ſo doubt, or diverſity take any thing, ſhall
r00622-00631 p006   alway reſort to the Biſhop of the Dioceſe, who by his diſcretion ſhall take order for the quieting and appeaſing of the ſame; ſo that the ſame order be not contrary to any thing
r00632-00632 p006   Of C E R E M O N I E S.
r00633-00635 p006   contained in this Book. And if the Biſhop of the Dioceſe be
r00636-00638 p006   in doubt, then he may ſend for the reſolution thereof to the
r00639-00640 p006   Archbiſhop.
r00641-00642 p006   H O U G H it be appointed, that all things ſhall be
r00643-00644 p006   read and ſung in the Church in the Engliſh Tongue,
r00645-00646 p006   to the end that the congregation may be thereby edified; yet it is not meant, but that when men ſay Morning and
r00647-00649 p006   Evening Prayer privately, they may ſay the ſame in any

r00678-00678 p006   F ſuch Ceremonies as be uſed in the Church, and have
r00679-00680 p006   had their beginning by the inſtitution of man, ſome at
r00681-00682 p006   the firſt were of godly intent and purpoſe deviſed, and yet at
r00683-00684 p006   length turned to vanity and ſuperſtition: Some entered into
r00685-00685 p006   the Church by undiſcreet devotion, and ſuch a zeal as was
r00686-00686 p006   without knowledge; and for becauſe they were winked at in
r00687-00687 p006   the beginning, they grew daily to more and more abuſes, which not only for their unprofitableneſs, but alſo becauſe
r00688-00689 p006   they have much blinded the people, and obſcured the glory of God, are worthy to be cut away, and clean rejected: other
r00690-00690 p006   there be, which although they have been deviſed by man, yet

r00692-00692 p006   “ “ “ “ “ “ “ “ “ “ “ “ O

r00695-00696 p007   it is thought good to reſerve them ſtill, as well for a decent
r00697-00698 p007   Order in the Church, (for the which they were firſt deviſed) as
r00699-00699 p007   becauſe they pertain to edification, whereunto all things done
r00700-00701 p007   in the Church (as the Apoſtle teacheth) ought to be referred.
r00702-00702 p007    And although the keeping or omitting of a Ceremony, in itſelf conſidered, is but a ſmall thing; yet the wilful and contemptuous tranſgreſſion and breaking of a common Order and Diſcipline is no ſmall offence before God, Let all things be
r00703-00704 p007   done among you, ſaith Saint Paul, in a ſeemly and due Order: The
r00705-00706 p007   appointment of the which Order pertaineth not to private men; therefore no man ought to take in hand, nor preſume to appoint or alter any publick or common Order in Chriſt's
r00707-00707 p007   Church, except he be lawfully called and authorized thereunto.  And whereas in this our time, the minds of men are ſo
r00708-00708 p007   diverſe, that ſome think it a great matter of Conſcience to
r00709-00710 p007   depart from a piece of the leaſt of their Ceremonies, they be ſo
r00711-00714 p007   addicted to their old cuſtoms: and again on the other ſide, ſome be ſo newfangled, that they would innovate all things,
r00715-00715 p007   and ſo deſpiſe the old, that nothing can like them, but that is
r00716-00718 p007   new: It was thought expedient, not ſo much to have reſpect how to pleaſe and ſatiſfy either of theſe parties, as how to
r00719-00721 p007   pleaſe God, and profit them both. And yet leſt any man ſhould be offended, whom good reaſon might ſatiſfy, here be
r00722-00724 p007   certain cauſes rendered, why ſome of the accuſtomed Ceremonies be put away, and ſome retained and kept ſtill.
r00725-00725 p007    Some are put away, becauſe the great exceſs and multitude
r00726-00726 p007   of them hath ſo increaſed in theſe latter days, that the burden
r00727-00727 p007   of them was intolerable; whereof St. Auguſtine in his time
r00728-00729 p007   complained, that they were grown to ſuch a number, that the eſtate of Chriſtian people was in worſe caſe concerning that
r00730-00730 p007   matter, than were the Jews. And he counſelled that ſuch yoke
r00731-00731 p007   and burden ſhould be taken away, as time would ſerve quietly
r00732-00732 p007   to do it. But what would St. Auguſtine have ſaid, if he had ſeen the Ceremonies of late days uſed among us; whereunto the multitude uſed in his time was not to be compared? This our exceſſive multitude of Ceremonies was ſo great, and many of
r00733-00733 p007   them ſo dark, that they did more confound and darken, than
r00734-00734 p007   Of C E R E M O N I E S.
r00735-00736 p007   declare and ſet forth Chriſt’s benefits unto us. And beſides
r00737-00738 p007   this, Chriſt’s Goſpel is not a Ceremonial Law, (as much of
r00739-00739 p007   Moſes' Law was,) but it is a Religion to ſerve God, not in
r00740-00740 p007   bondage of the figure or ſhadow, but in the freedom of the
r00741-00741 p007   Spirit; being content only with thoſe Ceremonies which do ſerve to a decent Order and godly Diſcipline, and ſuch as be
r00742-00743 p007   apt to ſtir up the dull mind of man to the remembrance of his
r00744-00744 p007   duty to God, by ſome notable and ſpecial ſignification,
r00745-00746 p007   whereby he might be edified. Furthermore, the moſt weighty
r00747-00747 p007   cauſe of the aboliſhment of certain Ceremonies was, That they
r00748-00749 p007   were ſo far abuſed, partly by the ſuperſtitious blindneſs of the
r00750-00751 p007   rude and unlearned, and partly by the unſatiable avarice of ſuch as ſought more their own lucre, than the glory of God,
r00752-00753 p007   that the abuſes could not well be taken away, the thing remaining ſtill.
r00754-00754 p007    But now as concerning thoſe Perſons, which peradventure

r00756-00757 p007   retained ſtill: If they conſider that without ſome Ceremonies it

r00760-00760 p007   judgements. And if they think much, that any of the old do remain, and would rather have all deviſed anew: then ſuch
r00761-00761 p007   men granting ſome Ceremonies convenient to be had, ſurely
r00762-00762 p007   where the old may be well uſed, there they cannot reaſonably
r00763-00763 p007   reprove the old only for their age, without bewraying of their own folly. For in ſuch a caſe they ought rather to have
r00764-00765 p007   reverence unto them for their Antiquity, if they will declare themſelves to be more ſtudious of Unity and Concord, than of
r00766-00766 p007   Innovations and New-fangleneſs, which (as much as may be
r00767-00768 p007   with the true ſetting forth of Chriſt’s Religion) is always to be
r00769-00770 p007   eſchewed. Furthermore, ſuch ſhall have no juſt cauſe with the
r00771-00771 p007   Ceremonies reſerved to be offended. For as thoſe be taken

For the Sacra- mental Bread and Wine remain ſtill in their very natural ſubſtances; and therefore may not be adored; (for that were Idolatry, to be abhorred of all faithful Chriſtians;) and the natural Body and Blood of our Saviour Chriſt are in Heaven, and not here; it being againſt the truth of Chriſt’s natural Body, to be at one time in more places than one.

r34153-34154 p332   which may nouriſh Faction both in the Church and Common-wealth. We

r34156-34156 p332   That the Articles of the Church of England (which have been allowed

r34163-34163 p332   the leaſt difference from the ſaid Articles; which to that end We command to be new printed, and this Our Declaration to be publiſhed therewith.

r34172-34172 p332   B

r34174-34175 p332    That out of our Princely Care, that the Churchmen may do the work which is proper unto them, the Biſhops and Clergy, from time to time, in Convocation, upon their humble deſire, ſhall have Licence under Our Broad
r34176-34179 p332   Seal, to deliberate of, and to do all ſuch things, as being made plain by them, and aſſented unto by Us, ſhall concern the ſettled continuance of the Doctrine

r34217-34218 p333   H E R E is but one living and true God, everlaſting,

r34233-34233 p333   II. Of the Word or Son of God, which was made very Man.
r34234-34235 p333   H E Son, which is the Word of the Father, begotten from everlaſting of the Father, the very and eternal

r34242-34245 p333   that two whole and perfect Natures, that is to ſay, the Godhead and the Manhood, were joined together in one Perſon,

r34350-34351 p334   RIGINAL Sin ſtandeth not in the following of Adam,

r34353-34355 p334   from original Righteouſneſs, and is of his own Nature inclined

r34500-34501 p335   XVII. Of Predeſtination and Election.
r34502-34504 p335   R E D E S T I N A T I O N to Life is the everlaſting purpoſe of God, whereby, before the foundations of the

r34527-34530 p335   adoption: they be made like the image of his only-begotten Son Jeſus Chriſt: they walk religiouſly in good works, and
r34531-34532 p335   at length, by God’s mercy, they attain to everlaſting felicity.
r34533-34535 p335    As the godly conſideration of Predeſtination, and our

r34555-34555 p335 D N P
r34556-34556 p335 H A R T I C L E S of R E L I G I O N.

r34575-34577 p335   unclean living, no leſs perilous than deſperation.
r34578-34582 p335    Furthermore, we muſt receive God's promiſes in ſuch wiſe,

r34586-34586 p335   XVIII. Of obtaining eternal Salvation only by the Name of Chriſt.

r34605-34605 p335   XIX. Of the Church.
r34606-34608 p335   H E viſible Church of Chriſt is a congregation of

r34615-34617 p335   are requiſite to the ſame.
r34618-34620 p335    As the Church of Hieruſalem, Alexandria, and Antioch, have erred; ſo alſo the Church of Rome hath erred, not only in their
r34621-34622 p335   living and manner of Ceremonies, but alſo in matters of Faith.
r34623-34623 p335   XX. Of the Authority of the Church.
r34624-34625 p335   HE Church hath power to decree Rites or Ceremonies, and authority in Controverſies of Faith: And yet it is

r34630-34635 p335   of holy Writ, yet, as it ought not to decree any thing againſt the ſame, ſo beſides the ſame ought it not to enforce
r34636-34636 p335   any thing to be believed for neceſſity of Salvation.

r34640-34640 p336   XXI. Of the Authority of General Councils.
r34641-34641 p336   E N E R A L Councils may not be gathered together without the commandment and will of princes. And
